item.title: National Guard Presence a 'Significant Investment' In DC Safety, Says Brig. Gen. Blanchard
item.description: Brigadier General Leland Blanchard II, Interim Commanding General of the DC National Guard, said that safety efforts in the 25 years since the September 11th terrorist attacks have been a balance between honoring personal liberties and the need for security. Brigadier General Blanchard also discussed his current mandate with the National Guard in DC and how his team works in coordination with the DC police, saying that it represents a 'significant investment' in the security of DC neighborhoods. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Scores of Young Sports Fans Placed Their First Bets This Summer
item.description: Bloomberg's Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." This summer’s FIFA World Cup packed stadiums across North America and drew record audiences. It also got a large number of millennials and Gen Zs to place their first sports bets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Must Think Of Wealth Transfers Differently: Zentner
item.description: Ellen Zentner, chief economic strategist and global head of thematic and macro investing at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how wealth managers must adjust to people living longer. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wealth Transfers Are Happening Later: Zentner
item.description: Ellen Zentner, chief economic strategist and global head of thematic and macro investing at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss financial planning, retirement, and the impact of growing life expectancy in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Should 'Deeply Value' Friendship of It's Allies, Says Former NATO Ambassador
item.description: Nicholas Burns, former Ambassador to NATO, reflected on the 25th anniversary of the September 11th and remembered the action of NATO countries in the days following the terror attacks, saying the US should 'deeply value' the friendship of its allies. Burns who also served as the US ambassador to China previewed the issues on the table ahead of President Xi's upcoming visit to the US and said the US, China and NATO allies 'need to be together in limiting the influence of AI when it comes to weapons of mass destruction.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Case Against Cutting Social Security: Kathryn Anne Edwards
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion's Kathryn Anne Edwards joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." Edwards writes that for the last 43 years Social Security has been on autopilot, and makes the case for modernizing the program to meet 2026 economic issues. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Americans Need To Come Together: Richard Haass
item.description: Richard Haass, senior counselor with Centerview Partners, president emeritus for the Council on Foreign Relations, and former advisor to Colin Powell and President George H.W. Bush, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." Sentiment sank among consumers from both political parties, according to a UMich survey, and only 35% of Republicans believe the government is doing a good job with the economy, the lowest reading since President Trump returned to the White House last year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: $40T Debt Is National Security Issue: Haass
item.description: Richard Haass, senior counselor with Centerview Partners, president emeritus for the Council on Foreign Relations, and former advisor to Colin Powell and President George H.W. Bush, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how American influence around the world affects the US consumer and their portfolios. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: RBC Hires Bank of America’s Dan Mills to Head Canada Rates Sales
item.description: Dan Mills is joining Royal Bank of Canada as a managing director and head of rates sales in Canada, according to a spokesperson.
item.dc:creator: Chunzi Xu

item.title: South East Water to Regroup on Debt Plan After Bond Talks Stall
item.description: South East Water Ltd. is reevaluating its plans to tap capital markets to raise debt, after initial talks with bond investors stalled over pricing.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Morpurgo, Ronan Martin and Laura Benitez

item.title: Pennsylvania Data Center Limits Are a Threat to Gas Firms, Trade Group Says
item.description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro’s new restrictions on data center development threaten a key source of demand growth for shale gas producers in the state, according to an industry trade group.
item.dc:creator: Julian Hast

item.title: Former NYR Goalie Henrik Lundqvist on Remembering 9/11
item.description: Romaine Bostick sat down with Henrik Lundqvist, former New York Rangers Goalie, from Cantor Fitzgerald's Charity Day, in remembrance of those who lost their lives in the September 11 attacks 25 years ago. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Allan Houston on Charity Efforts, NY Knicks Championship
item.description: Former New York Knick Allan Houston joins Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick at the Cantor Fitzgerald annual 9/11 Charity Day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nader Sisters on Remembering 9/11 and New TV Projects
item.description: Brooks Nader, Mary Holland Nader and Grace Anna Nader join Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick at the Cantor Fitzgerald annual 9/11 Charity Day. They reflect on Sept. 11, giving back with City Harvest and new projects they are working on. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Everyone Is Suddenly Talking About AI Safety
item.description: On today’s Big Take podcast: Two high-profile incidents in the AI industry prompt big questions about safety — and the future of humanity. Listen where’ve you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: In Post 9/11 Era, NYC's Downtown Forges Life Beyond Wall Street
item.description: Lower Manhattan has evolved from a business district that largely emptied out after work into a hub for housing, culture and nightlife, with the population more than doubling since 9/11. The area has added almost 25,000 residential units since 9/11, and its workforce has diversified, with financial services now representing 25% of downtown's occupied space. Blomberg's Amanda L. Gordon joins Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Marks 25 Years Since 9/11
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn and Michael Mckee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Twenty-five years after September 11th, America remembers. Kevin Hassett joins Open Interest on inflation, Fed independence and his memories of that day. Plus, Brandon and Kyle Lutnick on Cantor Fitzgerald’s legacy of giving after losing 658 colleagues. And Cantor Co-CEO Christian Wall on why the AI boom could unleash trillions in new debt. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Treasuries End Bruising Week With Fed Hike Bets Firmed After CPI
item.description: The $32 trillion US bond market ended a bruising week that pushed yields to multiyear highs, with investors more convinced the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to address sticky inflation.
item.dc:creator: Ye Xie and Greg Ritchie

item.title: Stocks Climb in Run-Up to Next Week’s Fed Decision: Markets Wrap
item.description: The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw stocks rising, with a decline in oil prices tempering concerns about inflationary pressures ahead of next week’s Federal Reserve decision.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 11
item.description: Brent oil dipped Friday but gained significantly overall for the week as the Iran war and threats against Saudi Arabia from Houthi militants keep traders on edge.
item.dc:creator: Bingyan Wang, Mia Gindis and Alex Longley
